newsitem.title: USA: Fed seen refraining from open market operations.
newsitem.headline: Fed seen refraining from open market operations.

text.p: The Federal Reserve will likely refrain from open market operations on Thursday, analysts said.

"With the eight-day (fixed system repurchase agreements) on the books, I don't think the need is pressing for them to come in today," said Kevin Flanagan, first vice president and money market economist at Dean Witter Reynolds Inc, though he added that there was an outside chance of "a round of customer" repurchases.
MMS International analysts also expect the Fed to stay out of the open market.
At 1130 EDT/1530 GMT, the time when the Fed usually intervenes in the market, the federal funds rate was quoted at a soft 5-3/16 percent, below the Fed's 5-1/4 percent target for the rate.
